Doctors follow HIPPA, and there are strict guidelines for how to configure various operating systems to comply with HIPPA's requirements.

FWIW: there is probably not any HIPPA guidance for Windows 8, let alone Windows 10 yet. Guidance very often lags the vendor's release by months, often years. So yes: if you're running Windows 10, you're very likely not in compliance with HIPPA. Run 7, and run the HIPPA guidance when configuring the machine - duh.
But enterprise versions will clearly have privacy controls. A standard desktop Windows 7 or 8 would have the same concerns

fwiw: you can apply almost all the same Security Policy stuff to a Windows 7 Home machine, (using a .inf template), as you can to Windows 7 ultimate; connected to a Domain Controller using Active Directory. The method of applying those settings is different, (you use the local security policy editor, rather than the Active Directory control panel, and pushing it out to the clients) - but pretty much all the settings that don't apply to domain users, can be set, including all the password restrictions, and encryption requirements.

It IS possible to lock down a standalone Windows 7 box - there's just no menu option to click on to get at the security policy editor, you have to run it at the command line. (or maybe it's in the "administrative tools" menu - I forget).

Those same tools are going to be on Windows 10; because the same underlying security database mechanism has to be on enterprise/ultimate editions, as the home edition. It's just a different interface, with more manual mucking around involved.

I think that's a good analogy. My other go-to comparison is the highway system. In the 1950s the U.S. government realized how important it is to have a connected road system and it funded a public build-out of roads across the nation. If the U.S. would do that for internet infrastructure, we would have dozens of ISPs competing on service instead of one or two big incumbents locking down the network. Right now the bus companies own the roads, and there's no reason to let other traffic on.
